diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Note that from now on we assume periodic boundary conditions. For this reason we set 
D_{1,2}^{x}= D_{1,N_x}^{x} &= 0\;,\qquad D_{N_x,N_x-1}^{x} = D_{N_x,1}^{x} = 0\;,\\
D_{1,1}^{xx}= 0\;, D_{1,2}^{xx} &=0\;,\qquad D_{N_x,N_x-1}^{xx} = 0\;, D_{N_x,N_x}^{xx} = 0.
D_{j,j\pm 1}^{x}= \frac{\pm 1}{2\Delta x}\;,\qquad D_{j,j}^{xx}= - \frac{2}{\left(\Delta x\right)^2}\;, \quad D_{j,j\pm 1}^{xx}= \frac{1}{\left(\Delta x\right)^2}\;,

issues.failure_explanation: The boundary entries are set to zero instead of using periodic wrap-around values. With these zero rows, D^x is not skew-symmetric and D^xx is not symmetric. For example, with N_x=3, D^x has row 1 and row 3 equal to zero, so for y=(0,1,0), z=(1,0,0), the left side of the first identity is -1/(2\Delta x) while the right side is 0. Thus the summation-by-parts properties stated in Lemma \ref{lemma:stencilmatrices} are false as written.

failure_location.quote: \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} y_j D_{ji}^x z_i = - \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} z_j D_{ji}^{x} y_i\;, \qquad \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} z_j D_{ji}^{x} z_i = 0 \;, \qquad \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} y_j D_{ji}^{xx} z_i = \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} z_j D_{ji}^{xx} y_i.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the zero boundary entries by proper periodic wrap-around entries (including corner entries for D^xx and D^+) so that the matrices become skew-symmetric/symmetric and satisfy the stated identities.
issues.overall_effect: The false summation-by-parts lemma invalidates Lemma \ref{lemma:fullydiscreteCFL} and the stability proofs that rely on it, including the stability of the full scheme and the DLRA scheme.
issues.title: Stencil matrices violate claimed summation-by-parts properties
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local correction of boundary entries; the method, CFL condition, and stability claims survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: f_{jk}^{n+1} = f_{jk}^n - \Delta t  \sum_{i=1}^{N_x} D_{ji}^x f_{ik}^n v_k.

issues.failure_explanation: The scheme is explicit Euler with centered spatial differences for advection. Its amplification factor is G = 1 - i (v \Delta t/\Delta x) \sin(k \Delta x), so |G|^2 = 1 + (v \Delta t/\Delta x)^2 \sin^2(k \Delta x) > 1 for every \Delta t>0 and nonzero modes. Hence it is unconditionally unstable, not stable for small time steps.

failure_location.quote: Indeed, one can show that the discretization given in \eqref{eq:EH-Counterexample} is not von Neumann stable, but stable for relatively small time step sizes \cite{leveque2002}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the sentence to state that the scheme is unconditionally unstable, or remove the claim that it is stable for small time step sizes.
issues.overall_effect: The sentence incorrectly describes the stability property of the naive scheme. It is a local false statement used only for motivation and does not affect the main stable scheme.
issues.title: False prose claim about stability of the naive centered scheme
issues.why_classification: The error is a short prose correction with no impact on the paper's main results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let us assume that the initial condition for $g$ satisfies $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \sum_{k=1}^{N_v} g_{jk}^0 \omega_k e^{v_k^2/2} = 1$.
From Lemma \ref{lemma:fullydiscrete-rho} we have that $\sum_{k=1}^{N_v} f_{jk}^{n+1} \omega_k e^{v_k^2} = \rho_j^{n+1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem \ref{theorem:stabilityMg} uses Lemma \ref{lemma:fullydiscrete-rho}, which requires the discrete moment condition on the initial g. The theorem statement does not include this assumption. Without it, the relation \sum f^n \omega e^{v^2} = \rho^n may fail, and the collision term in the stability proof is not guaranteed to be dissipative.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the initial moment-condition assumption to the theorem statements (and ensure it is preserved by the scheme).
issues.overall_effect: The stability guarantee is only established for initial data satisfying the discrete moment condition; the stated theorem overclaims stability for arbitrary initial data.
issues.title: Missing initial moment-condition hypothesis in stability theorem
issues.why_classification: The fix is a standard consistency assumption that is already used in the proof; it preserves the stability result under the intended setup.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: g_{jk}^{n+1} \left(1+\sigma \Delta t \right) =& \ \frac{\rho_j^n}{\rho_j^{n+1}} g_{jk}^n -\Delta t \sum_{i=1}^{N_x} \frac{1}{\rho_j^{n+1}} D_{ji}^x \left(\rho_i^n g_{ik}^n \right) v_k + \Delta t \frac{\Delta x}{2} \sum_{i=1}^{N_x} \frac{1}{\rho_j^{n+1}} D_{ji}^{xx} \left(\rho_i^n g_{ik}^n \right) |v_k| + \sigma \Delta t,
Note that the scattering term $\left(1+\sigma \Delta t \right)$ is only applied in the $S$-step as it does not affect the span of the basis functions derived in the $K$- and $L$-step.

issues.failure_explanation: The full update equation has the factor (1+\sigma\Delta t) multiplying g^{n+1}. The S-step correctly divides by this factor. However, the K-step (and similarly the L-step) includes the source term +\sigma\Delta t \sum V but does not have (1+\sigma\Delta t) on the left. This is inconsistent: either the collision term should be omitted from K/L (as the text says scattering is only applied in the S-step), or the left side must be (1+\sigma\Delta t)K^{n+1}. As written, the basis update solves a different equation from the intended split.

failure_location.quote:
K_{jp}^{n+1} =& \ \frac{\rho_j^n}{\rho_j^{n+1}} K_{jp}^n -\Delta t \frac{1}{\rho_j^{n+1}} \sum_{i=1}^{N_x} D_{ji}^x \rho_i^n \sum_{\ell=1}^r K_{i\ell}^n \sum_{k=1}^{N_v} V_{k\ell}^n v_k V_{kp}^n\nonumber\\
&+ \Delta t \frac{\Delta x}{2} \frac{1}{\rho_j^{n+1}} \sum_{i=1}^{N_x} D_{ji}^{xx} \rho_i^n \sum_{\ell=1}^r K_{i\ell}^n \sum_{k=1}^{N_v} V_{k\ell}^n |v_k| V_{kp}^n+ \sigma \Delta t \sum_{k=1}^{N_v} V_{kp}^n.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the +\sigma\Delta t terms from the K- and L-steps, or add the missing (1+\sigma\Delta t) factor to their left-hand sides consistently with the S-step.
issues.overall_effect: The DLRA algorithm as written is not the algorithm whose stability is proved; its K- and L-steps produce incorrect basis updates.
issues.title: Inconsistent collision treatment in DLRA K- and L-steps
issues.why_classification: The error is a concrete defect in the algorithm construction. The repair is local but changes the basis-update equations, so it is more than a pure typo.

issues.failure_explanation: The identity \sum P^X_{\alpha j} g_{\alpha\beta}(\rho_\alpha)^2 = g_{j\beta}(\rho_j)^2 holds only if diag(\rho^2) g_{\cdot\beta} lies in the span of \doublehat X. The augmentation \doublehat X = qr([\hat X, (\rho^2)\hat X]) ensures this for vectors in span(\hat X), but g^{n+1} lies in span(\doublehat X), which contains additional directions. Multiplication by \rho^2 can take such a vector out of the span. A similar failure occurs for the velocity identity with weight \omega e^{v^2/2}. Thus the claimed identities are not guaranteed by the stated augmentation, and the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:added-1} is invalid.

failure_location.quote: \sum_{\alpha=1}^{N_x} P_{\alpha j}^{X} g_{\alpha \beta}^{n+1} (\rho_\alpha^{n+1})^2 = g_{j \beta}^{n+1} (\rho_j^{n+1})^2 \quad \text{ and } \quad \sum_{\beta=1}^{N_v} P_{k\beta}^{V} g_{j\beta}^{n+1} \omega_\beta e^{v_\beta^2/2} = g_{jk}^{n+1} \omega_k e^{v_k^2/2}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the basis augmentation so that the relevant spans are invariant under multiplication by the weights, or supply a different proof that the required weighted projection identities hold for the computed solution.
issues.overall_effect: The rigorous stability proof for the DLRA scheme fails. The claim that the rank-4r augmentation ensures the needed projection identities and preserves the moment condition is unsupported.
issues.title: DLRA stability proof relies on invalid projection identities from insufficient basis augmentation
issues.why_classification: The main DLRA stability theorem is unsupported. Repairing the proof requires a new argument or a more substantial augmentation strategy, not a local correction.
